fact_checks.current_value: Focal; Primary generalized tonic-clonic; LGS; Generalized
fact_checks.proposed_value: Focal; Primary generalized tonic-clonic; LGS; Generalized
fact_checks.rationale: FDA indications support partial-onset seizures, primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. The broader "Generalized" filter is acceptable only as a roll-up category for PGTC/LGS, not as all generalized epilepsies.

fact_checks.current_value: Precise anticonvulsant mechanism is unknown; preclinical effects include voltage-dependent sodium-channel blockade, GABA-A augmentation, AMPA/kainate antagonism, and carbonic-anhydrase inhibition.
fact_checks.proposed_value: Precise anticonvulsant mechanism is unknown; preclinical effects include voltage-dependent sodium-channel blockade, GABA-A augmentation, AMPA/kainate antagonism, and carbonic-anhydrase inhibition.
fact_checks.rationale: The FDA label states the precise mechanisms are unknown and lists these four preclinical properties.
The mechanism is supported by FDA labeling; the row should cite the FDA label directly rather than mixed FDA/DailyMed wording.

fact_checks.current_value: Weak CYP3A inducer at higher doses; inhibits CYP2C19; weak carbonic anhydrase inhibitor
fact_checks.proposed_value: Mild CYP3A4 inducer; mild CYP2C19 inhibitor; weak carbonic anhydrase inhibitor
fact_checks.rationale: FDA labeling states in vitro topiramate is a mild CYP2C19 inhibitor and mild CYP3A4 inducer, and mechanism labeling states carbonic anhydrase inhibition.

fact_checks.proposed_value: Not extensively metabolized; primarily renal elimination unchanged in urine; minor hepatic metabolism via hydroxylation, hydrolysis, and glucuronidation
fact_checks.rationale: FDA labeling says topiramate is not extensively metabolized and about 70% is eliminated unchanged in urine; the current wording is directionally correct but less precise.
FDA labeling gives a mean elimination half-life of 21 hours; NCBI/PubMed pharmacokinetic sources support an approximate 19-25 hour range, so 19-23 h is acceptable.

fact_checks.current_value: 400 mg/day for most adult epilepsy indications; up to 1000 mg/day in older adjunctive labeling
fact_checks.proposed_value: 400 mg/day for current FDA-approved adult epilepsy indications; adult adjunctive partial-onset/LGS dosing is 200-400 mg/day, adult adjunctive PGTC and monotherapy dosing is 400 mg/day, and doses above 400 mg/day have not been shown to improve adult partial-onset responses.
fact_checks.rationale: Current FDA labeling supports 400 mg/day as the adult epilepsy dose ceiling for labeled use. The "up to 1000 mg/day" phrase reflects older trial dose-ranging, not a current approved daily dose statement in the cited current FDA label.

fact_checks.current_value: 200 mg/day common adult epilepsy maintenance target
fact_checks.proposed_value: 200 mg/day common adult adjunctive partial-onset/LGS maintenance target
fact_checks.rationale: FDA labeling gives 200-400 mg/day for adult adjunctive partial-onset seizures or LGS, and the Guberman 2002 RCT supports 200 mg/day efficacy.

fact_checks.current_value: Adults epilepsy: 200-400 mg/day divided or once daily XR; higher for some adjunctive regimens
fact_checks.proposed_value: Adults epilepsy: 200-400 mg/day; immediate-release products are generally given in two divided doses and extended-release products once daily.
fact_checks.rationale: The current FDA label supports 200-400 mg/day adult adjunctive partial-onset/LGS dosing and 400 mg/day adult PGTC/monotherapy dosing. The "higher" phrase is not supported as current typical approved dosing.

fact_checks.current_value: Neurologic: paresthesia 51%, CNS: somnolence 29%, CNS: dizziness 25%, cognitive: psychomotor slowing 21%, constitutional: fatigue 16%, metabolic: weight loss 16%
fact_checks.proposed_value: Adult adjunctive epilepsy, FDA recommended-dose pooled trials: CNS: somnolence 29%, CNS: dizziness 25%, constitutional: fatigue 15%, cognitive: psychomotor slowing 13%, neurologic: paresthesia 11%, metabolic: weight loss 9%
fact_checks.rationale: The current values mix percentages from different dose/indication contexts and are not supported as a coherent set by the current FDA label table for adult adjunctive epilepsy at 200-400 mg/day.

fact_checks.current_value: No clinically meaningful QT effect established
fact_checks.proposed_value: No clinically meaningful QT prolongation established
fact_checks.rationale: FDA review material for topiramate extended-release states it does not prolong QT interval, with the caveat that the study lacked a positive control to qualify as a full ICH E14 thorough QT study.

missing_rcts.title: Once-daily USL255 as adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures: randomized phase III study.
missing_rcts.why_relevant: USL255 is Qudexy XR/topiramate extended-release. PREVAIL was a global phase III randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled adjunctive trial in refractory partial-onset seizures, so it is same-active-drug RCT evidence and should not be omitted because the alias differs from generic topiramate.

missing_rcts.title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of topiramate in adults with epilepsy and intellectual disability: impact on seizures, severity, and quality of life.
missing_rcts.why_relevant: This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled adjunctive topiramate epilepsy trial. It appears underpowered/negative and does not add extractable maximum-effective-dose outcome values, but it qualifies for the PubMed RCT link list.

outcome_checks.proposed_value: 14.7-43 % (drug minus placebo RR50 differential at maximum effective dose/regimen; add Chung2014 USL255/topiramate ER 200 mg/day 14.7% to the existing verified entries)
outcome_checks.rationale: Existing immediate-release topiramate RR50 differentials are supported by the cited RCT abstracts/tables, but the same-drug USL255/Qudexy XR phase III RCT reports an extractable placebo-adjusted RR50 differential of 37.9% minus 23.2% = 14.7%, which changes the minimum of the range.

outcome_checks.proposed_value: 17.9-58 % (drug minus placebo MPC differential at maximum effective dose/regimen; add Chung2014 USL255/topiramate ER 200 mg/day 17.9% to the existing verified entries)
outcome_checks.rationale: Existing immediate-release median percent-change differentials are supported, but FDA review/USL255 trial evidence reports median seizure-frequency reduction of 39.50% with USL255 versus 21.65% with placebo, differential 17.85% rounded to 17.9%, changing the minimum range.

rct_link_checks.label: Zhang2011
rct_link_checks.rationale: Topiramate adjunctive therapy; randomized placebo-controlled trial in refractory partial epilepsy in elderly patients; RR50 outcome supports the row.

rct_link_checks.label: Novotny2010
rct_link_checks.rationale: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized infant refractory partial-onset seizure trial; negative/non-effective and appropriately not used in maximum-effective outcome plots.

rct_link_checks.label: Guberman2002
rct_link_checks.rationale: Double-blind placebo-controlled randomized trial of topiramate 200 mg/day; median reduction 44% versus 20% placebo supports MPC differential 24%.

rct_link_checks.label: Yen2000
rct_link_checks.rationale: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled adjunctive topiramate trial; RR50 47.8% versus 13.0% supports differential 34.8%.

rct_link_checks.label: Sachdeo1999
rct_link_checks.rationale: Multicenter double-blind placebo-controlled randomized LGS trial; drop-attack MPC 14.8% versus -5.1% and major-seizure RR50 33% versus 8% support row values.

rct_link_checks.rationale: Multicenter double-blind placebo-controlled randomized partial epilepsy trial; MPC, RR50, and seizure-freedom values match the row.

rct_link_checks.label: Elterman1999

rct_link_checks.label: Biton1999
